page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6a.large is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an AMD EPYC 7H12 processor running at a base clock speed of 2.6 GHz. The instance is configured with 2 dedicated physical cores, 2 vCPUs, and 1.0 thread per core. It includes 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate that the ecs.g6a.large sits primarily in the lower performance tiers for intensive tasks. Its stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU performance scores of 766.59 fall into the bottom 10% category. Similarly, its Geekbench multi-core score of 1566.0 and Passmark CPU score of 2792.75 are rated as poor. Memory bandwidth tests show weak to poor performance, with read-only large block bandwidth at 23.06 GB/sec and write large block bandwidth at 15.78 GB/sec. However, single-threaded bzip3 decompression and Geekbench single-core performance achieve average ratings, scoring 9.2 GB/sec and 1280.0 respectively.

Given its hardware profile, the ecs.g6a.large offers an entry-level general-purpose resource allocation. The absence of local storage and dedicated GPUs, combined with lower-tier benchmark results in database operations and static web serving, suggests significant performance tradeoffs for high-throughput applications. It is qualitatively positioned as a budget-friendly option for workloads with low resource demands. Appropriate workloads include basic web serving, lightweight application testing, simple text processing, and general-purpose utility tasks that do not require high computational density or rapid memory access.
